nodes.label: Navigable Space
nodes.description: A key cultural form of new media alongside the database, characterized by spatial constructions that can be computed, transmitted, and navigated as a trajectory. Functions as an interface to data and a new media type in itself.

nodes.label: Database
nodes.description: The complementary supermodern form to navigable space, representing the flattening of narrative into an unstructured collection of items.

nodes.label: Computer Space
nodes.description: Virtual 3D environments generated by computers, often characterized by separate objects rather than a continuous spatial medium.

nodes.label: Aggregate Space
nodes.description: A discontinuous space composed of discrete entities, objects, or levels, lacking a unified systematic perspective (akin to ancient Greek space). Typical of the Web and virtual worlds.

nodes.label: Systematic Space
nodes.description: Infinite, homogeneous, continuous space that exists prior to objects, associated with Renaissance perspective.

nodes.label: Space-Medium
nodes.description: The concept of an environment where objects and space are embedded into an inseparable dense field (prostranstvennaya sreda), lacking distinct rigid boundaries.

nodes.label: The Flâneur
nodes.description: The modern urban observer who finds home in the anonymous crowd, navigating city spaces; reincarnated in new media as the Net surfer or Data Dandy.

nodes.label: The Explorer
nodes.description: The lonely hero navigating wilderness or unknown territories to build character and map space; reincarnated in new media as the player of computer games.

nodes.label: Flight Simulator
nodes.description: A military training technology that historically pioneered the interactive navigation of simulated spatial environments.

nodes.label: Non-place
nodes.description: Spaces of transit, contractuality, and impermanence (e.g., airports, highways, Web navigation) produced by supermodernity, animated by trajectories of moving bodies.

nodes.label: Supermodernity
nodes.description: A contemporary condition characterized by trajectories, flows, databases, and non-places, superseding modern forms of narrative and stable architecture.
